name: Pensacola
note: One fluff pulp machine permanently shut in 2023; the mill still runs.

name: Riegelwood
note: One pulp machine permanently shut at the end of 2023.

name: Franklin
note: Paper making ended in 2010; fluff pulp production continues.

name: Longview (Nippon Dynawave)
note: Largely shut after the May 2026 white-liquor tank collapse; long-term status unresolved.

name: Lufkin
note: Southland Paper Mills; early newsprint from southern pine.

name: Camas
note: Pulping ended; a reduced paper operation remained.

name: Augusta sawmill
note: Closed 2025 per Forisk's 2025 producer rankings.

name: Estill sawmill
note: Closed 2025 per Forisk's 2025 producer rankings.

name: Darlington sawmill
note: Closed 2025 per Forisk's 2025 producer rankings.

name: Glenwood sawmill
note: Closed 2025 per Forisk's 2025 producer rankings.

name: 100 Mile House sawmill
note: Canadian, not US -- included for context on 2025 closure wave; verify before mapping if US-only view is needed.

name: Henderson sawmill
note: Expanded in 2025; capacity increase not separately quantified in source.

name: Angelina sawmill
note: Acquired by West Fraser in 2021; designed for roughly 700,000 m3/yr (~300 MMBF) at full capacity.

name: Fulton sawmill
note: Canfor completed a capacity investment here in 2025 (amount not disclosed in source).

name: Jasper sawmill
note: Expansion advanced in 2025; new capacity not disclosed in source.

name: Ackerman sawmill
note: Expansion with STP completed 2025; new capacity not disclosed in source.

name: Dodson sawmill
note: Modernization project completed 2025; capacity not disclosed in source.

name: Meldrim sawmill
note: One of four Simpson Lumber mills Interfor acquired in 2014; combined capacity of the four was 750 MMBF/yr.

name: Camas panel/paper complex
note: Listed separately from the pulp entry; pulping ended in 2018, some paper operation continued after.

name: Waco recycled paper mill
note: New $1B recycled containerboard mill, targeted Q4 2025 startup.

name: Morrilton expansion
note: ~$1B expansion adding a new continuous digester and chip mill, could more than double pulping capacity.

name: Taylorsville Plywood
note: GP company history places first southern pine plywood production here in the 1960s; exact year not specified in sources.

name: Prosperity Plywood
note: $14 million upgrade investment announced in 2025.

name: Gurdon Plywood
note: Built by International Paper in 1979; GP acquired it in 2006 along with Corrigan/Camden TX plywood mills; $70M upgrade announced 2019.

name: Emporia Plywood
note: Permanently closed May-July 2025 amid a housing/remodel demand slump; 550+ jobs lost.

name: Coquille Plywood
note: Now Roseburg's primary specialty softwood plywood operation after 2025 veneer-production consolidation.

name: Dillard Plywood (hardwood line)
note: Oldest plant in the Roseburg enterprise; hardwood plywood line closed Sept 2025 as the company exited hardwood plywood, though other Dillard operations (lumber, new MDF plant) continue.

name: Oakdale Plywood
note: Originally built by Vancouver Plywood Inc., which relocated from Washington state to build sister plants at Oakdale and Florien.

name: Florien Plywood
note: Sister plant to Oakdale, both built by Vancouver Plywood Inc. in 1965.

name: Chester Plywood
note: Built in the 1980s (exact year not specified); had multiple owners before Boise Cascade reacquired it in 2013.

name: Havana Plywood (Coastal)
note: Formerly Coastal Plywood/Coastal Forest Resources Company, founded 1980; Boise Cascade acquired it for $512M in 2022 along with the Chapman, AL mill.

name: Chapman Plywood (Coastal)
note: Formerly Coastal Plywood/Coastal Forest Resources Company, founded 1980; Boise Cascade acquired it for $512M in 2022 along with the Havana, FL mill.

name: Wiggins Plywood
note: Started up in 1971 by International Paper; Hood Industries acquired it in 1984. Closure announced 2026 following Tropical Storm Arthur damage and the facility's age.

name: Beaumont Plywood
note: New $216M laminated-plywood facility replacing one damaged by an April 2022 tornado, built at roughly 2x the prior capacity; groundbreaking May 2023, production targeted for early 2025.

name: Kalispell Plywood
note: Originally C&C Plywood Corp.; purchased by Plum Creek Manufacturing in the late 1970s, became a Weyerhaeuser mill after the 2016 Plum Creek merger.

name: Sagola OSB
note: Also produces LP SmartSide siding; OSB capacity approx. 410 MMSF/yr (3/8-in basis).

name: Thomasville OSB
note: Clarke County mill; had a serious fire during 2008 startup; capacity approx. 750 MMSF/yr (3/8-in basis).

name: Easton OSB
note: Huber's original 1983 OSB plant, the foundation of today's Huber Engineered Woods brand.

name: Crystal Hill OSB
note: 978-acre site; produces ZIP System and AdvanTech structural panels.

name: Spring City OSB
note: Opened 1997; idled in 2011 amid the housing downturn; reopened with production restarting in April 2018.

name: Broken Bow OSB
note: $130M mill; capacity approx. 600 MMSF/yr.

name: Cohasset OSB
note: $440M sixth Huber Engineered Woods mill announced 2021; construction began spring 2022 with an approx. 2.5-year build; exact production-start date not confirmed in sources.

name: Allendale OSB
note: Built by Georgia-Pacific, began OSB production in 2007; West Fraser acquired it for approx. $280M in Dec 2021; capacity approx. 760 MMSF/yr (3/8-in basis).

name: Huguley OSB
note: West Fraser restarted this previously idled OSB mill in 2017; original construction date under prior ownership unclear.

name: Jefferson OSB
note: West Fraser restarted this previously idled OSB mill in 2013; original construction date under prior ownership unclear.

name: Fordyce OSB
note: A distinct OSB line at the same site as GP's original 1964 Fordyce plywood mill (the first southern pine plywood plant in the world), which was permanently closed in 2009.

name: Hosford OSB
note: Construction began around 2002; first shipment came in 2005.

name: Sutton OSB
note: Marketed as the 'Sutton' mill though located in Heaters, Braxton County; site selection began 1993-94, mill opened in the mid-to-late 1990s (exact year not confirmed in sources).

name: Grayling Particleboard
note: $450M plant with North America's largest-capacity continuous single-line particleboard press plus two TFL lines; began production in late 2018.

name: Moncure MDF
note: Originally Uniboard's MDF/HDF plant (North America's largest at its Feb 2010 launch); Arauco acquired the site in 2012 and closed the co-located particleboard line in April 2020, retaining MDF/millwork operations.

name: Eastaboga Particleboard
note: New Siempelkamp particleboard line (first board Oct 9, 2019) on a site that also hosts a 329,000 m3/yr MDF line; particleboard capacity approx. 550,000 m3/yr; $463M total site investment.

name: Medford MDF
note: Known as Medite; 2024 press materials describe it as part of the Rogue Valley community for 49 years, implying a mid-1970s start; exact year not confirmed.

name: Malvern MDF
note: Earliest documented ownership is Willamette Industries in 1986; passed to Flakeboard in 2006, then Arauco in 2012. Exact original construction year not confirmed.

name: Adel Particleboard
note: Built by Weyerhaeuser in 1968; sold to SierraPine in 1999; permanently closed 2014.

name: Eugene MDF
note: Described as 50 years old in a 2006 article, implying a mid-1950s start (exact year not confirmed); Weyerhaeuser sold it to Flakeboard in 2006, Arauco acquired Flakeboard in 2012 and closed the plant May 1, 2020.

name: Dillard MDF
note: New MDF plant (separate from Roseburg's long-running Dillard plywood/lumber complex) targeted to start up in late summer 2024 as part of a $700M+ southern Oregon investment.

name: El Dorado MDF
note: Built 1998 as Del-Tin Fiber, a PotlatchDeltic subsidiary; Roseburg purchased the plant for $92 million, completed February 2019.

name: Axis Sawmill
note: New $210M sawmill replacing older Mobile-area capacity; opened end of 2024; capacity approx. 250 MMBF/yr.

name: Waldo Sawmill
note: $131M expansion/modernization completed 2024.

name: Warren Sawmill
note: $27M new mill built 1994 at a site Potlatch had operated since acquiring Bradley Lumber Co. in 1956; capacity approx. 220 MMBF/yr.

name: Ola Sawmill
note: One of three PotlatchDeltic Southern yellow pine mills in Arkansas, along with Waldo and Warren.

name: Hermanville Sawmill
note: Founded as Southern Lumber Company in 1983; Canfor acquired it for approx. $48.7M in 2015.

name: Camden Sawmill
note: In operation since 1983; $40M upgrade completed 2018.

name: Conway Sawmill
note: Built in 1957; one of four New South Companies plants Canfor acquired in 2006.

name: Laclede Sawmill
note: Began operations Sept 30, 1976; became part of Idaho Forest Group via the 2008 merger of Riley Creek Lumber and Bennett Forest Industries.

name: Arcata Sawmill
note: Built on the Samoa Peninsula starting in the early 1950s; permanently closed January 2016 amid a timber-supply falloff and rising Canadian imports, over 100 jobs lost.

name: Dierks Sawmill
note: Original Dierks Lumber & Coal Co. mill dated to 1918; Weyerhaeuser purchased Dierks Forests in 1969; replaced on-site by a new $190M facility completed 2018 with capacity approx. 380 MMBF/yr.

name: Millport Sawmill
note: Produces 2x4x8 studs; in operation since 1973.

name: Barnwell
note: Orchids Paper Products built a 110-in Valmet tissue machine here, installed 2016; Cascades acquired the mill in 2019 and closed it in 2023 amid restructuring; site was later reacquired and reopened in 2025 by ST Group as Barnwell Tissue Solutions.

name: Cheboygan
company: Tissue Depot (formerly Great Lakes Tissue Co.)
note: Great Lakes Tissue Co. began making 100% recycled towels/tissue at this site (which had paper-mill roots back to 1915) in 1993; operated later as Tissue Depot under Patriot Advanced Environmental Technologies, which was ordered by a federal court to shut its papermaking equipment amid litigation, then a Sept. 2023 warehouse fire ended operations for good.

name: Cosmopolis
note: Weyerhaeuser converted the former lumber-mill site into a dissolving/specialty cellulose pulp mill in 1957; production was shut down in Dec. 2022 under owner Cosmo Specialty Fibers; EPA later conducted a hazardous-chemical removal at the dormant site.

name: Hutchinson
note: Paperboard mill opened 1909; Sonoco (owner since 2001, via acquisition from Republic Group) abruptly closed the 90,000-ton/yr mill in March 2023, laying off 116 workers.

name: Old Town
note: Historic Penobscot River pulp mill (papermaking here dates to 1882) was shuttered by prior owner Expera in 2015; ND Paper/Nine Dragons bought the site in 2018 and restarted it as a recycled bleached-kraft pulp mill in 2019; idled indefinitely in April 2023 citing high fiber and energy costs and has not restarted since.

name: Putney
company: Marcal Paper Mills, Inc. (previously Soundview Paper Company)
note: Tissue-making at this Sacketts Brook site dates to 1869 (Eagle Paper Mill), on a mill site used for papermaking since the early 1800s; operated most recently as Soundview/Putney Paper (Marcal brand), producing recycled tissue parent rolls; papermaking stopped Jan. 16, 2024 (the separate converting operation ran a few more weeks) after energy costs became unsustainable.

name: Saint Helens
note: St. Helens Pulp and Paper Mill was built by Crown Zellerbach (its 50th anniversary was marked in 1977); Cascades began recycled-tissue production at the site in 2002; Cascades shut its remaining paper machine and fully closed the plant in Oct. 2023 amid weak West Coast demand for brown recycled tissue.

name: South Glens Falls
note: Tissue mill on the Hudson River built 1883-84; Essity abruptly closed it in July 2023, consolidating US tissue production at other sites and affecting roughly 300 area jobs.

name: Sumner
note: Uncoated recycled paperboard (URB) mill running since 1915 (Sonoco-owned since 1980); Sonoco permanently closed the 40,000-ton/yr mill effective Feb. 5, 2024, citing network optimization.

name: Tacoma
note: Kraft pulp and paper mill (linerboard, kraft bag paper) built 1929 by St. Regis Paper Co.; passed through Champion, Simpson Paper and RockTenn to WestRock; WestRock permanently closed the 510,000-ton/yr mill in Sept. 2023 after 94 years, citing high operating costs.

name: Tama
note: Paperboard mill opened 1878 (originally straw-based, later 100% recycled box board); Graphic Packaging closed the small, high-cost-per-ton mill on June 2, 2023, after 144+ years, as part of a network simplification.

name: Port Angeles (Nippon Paper)
company: Grupo Bio PAPPEL, S.A.B. de C.V. (McKinley Paper Co.)
note: A genuinely distinct facility from the Rayonier pulp mill (1930-1997) elsewhere in Port Angeles: this integrated pulp/paper mill at Ediz Hook was built in 1920 by Crown Zellerbach, passed to Daishowa America (1988) and then Nippon Paper Industries; Nippon sold it to McKinley Paper Co. (a Grupo Bio Pappel subsidiary) in 2017, and McKinley permanently closed the mill in mid-2024 (60-day WARN notice issued late June 2024) citing recovered-paper costs and weak demand.

name: Westervelt (Gulf States Paper)
company: Westervelt Co. (formerly Gulf States Paper Corp.)
note: Built by Gulf States Paper Corp. as Alabama's first paper mill; made bleached kraft pulp and paper; in operation about 50 years before closing in the mid-1970s (exact year not confirmed, hence 1975 estimate). Parent company continued as Westervelt Co. in forest products/real estate after the mill closed.

name: Crossett
note: Kraft pulp/paper mill built 1937 by Crossett Lumber Co.; Georgia-Pacific bought the site in 1962. Bleached board production ended in 2019 with a shift toward tissue/towel, but the pulp mill and chemical plant continue operating.

name: Los Angeles Paper Box & Board Mill
company: Los Angeles Paper Box & Board Mills Inc.
note: Family-owned recycled paperboard mill and folding-carton/box plant; still operating in Commerce, CA (LA metro area).

name: Simkins Industries (New Haven Pulp & Paper)
note: Originally New Haven Pulp & Paper Co.; recycled old newspapers into paperboard and specialty papers (Deerfield Specialty Papers & Glassine Canada brand). Permanently closed on or about Aug. 25, 2006 after years of losses and a failed contract-concession vote.

name: Atlas Paper Mills
company: Atlas Paper Mills Ltd. (Atlas Paper Mills LLC)
note: Founded by Remberto Bastanzuri, a Cuban paper-industry veteran who arrived in Miami in 1979; sources differ on the exact founding year (1979-1982). Recycled-fiber tissue mill actually located in Hialeah (Miami-Dade County), not a specific city named in the old directory; still operating.

name: Roses SouthEast Papers
note: Recycled/virgin tissue mill (bath tissue, towels, napkins); acquired by a Peak Rock Capital affiliate in 2014 and rebranded Atlas Southeast Papers; still operating.

name: Caraustar Austell
note: 100%-recycled paperboard mill built 1947; Caraustar was headquartered here for decades. Greif acquired Caraustar in 2019; the mill is still operating.
